original: C++ TEMPLATE VERSION OF Robert J. Jenkins Jr.'s ISAAC Random Number Generator. Ported from vanilla C to to template C++ class by Quinn Tyler Jackson on 16-23 July 1998. qjackson@wave.home.com The function for the expected period of this random number generator, according to Jenkins is: f(a,b) = 2**((a+b*(3+2^^a)-1) (where a is ALPHA and b is bitwidth) So, for a bitwidth of 32 and an ALPHA of 8, the expected period of ISAAC is: 2^^(8+32*(3+2^^8)-1) = 2^^8295 Jackson has been able to run implementations with an ALPHA as high as 16, or 2^^2097263

original: *********************************************************************** I use the following procedure in TC to generate seeds: The sow() procedure calculates two seeds for use with the random number generator from the system clock. I decided how to do this myself, and I am sure that there must be better ways to select seeds; hopefully, however, this is good enough. The first seed is calculated from the values for second, minute, hour, and year-day; weighted with the second most significant and year-day least significant. The second seed weights the values in reverse. **************************
pt: *********************************************************************** eu usar the seguinte procedimento em TC para gerar seeds: The sow() procedimento calcula dois seeds para usar com o aleatorio numero gerador do sistema relogio. eu decided como para fazer este eu mesmo, and eu am certo de que la deve ser melhor ways para selecionar seeds; hopefully, porem, este e bom suficiente. The primeiro semente e calculado do valores para segundo, minute, hour, and ano-dia; ponderado com o segundo mais significativo and ano-dia menos significativo. The segundo semente pesos the valores em reverso. **************************
